title: Q-STD-conventional-commits: bring the eight baseline commit titles to the Conventional Commits header
body:
**Owner:** executor
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation standards --adopted conventional-commits-semver
**Status:** closed

`python3 -m foundation standards --commits` holds every commit title a workflow or script generates to `<type>[(scope)][!]: <description>`. Eight titles are on the shrink-only baseline in doctrine/commit-convention.json because another program or record matches their text: `executor provenance` (foundation/queue.py), `backup drill record` (scripts/smoke_live.py), `REGEN-1: regenerate generated files` (scripts/regen_generated.sh) and the intent-yield, product-manager, seed-launch, temporal and tenant-repos workflow titles. For each, change the generator and its reader in one change (for example `executor: provenance`, `backup-drill: record (BLINDSPOT-1)`), remove the baseline entry and lower `baseline_ceiling`. Also read the titles built in JavaScript and from shell variables (the lane, the queue, deploy-ultrastable), which the lint does not see yet: add their files to `generators` once the titles are literals the lint can read.

STANDARDS-FIRST-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): "Standards, don't reinvent the wheel. Apply standards." The row is `conventional-commits-semver` in seed/standards/standards.json; this item closes when that row reads `"adoption": "adopted"` and every probe on it passes. Change the row in the same change that makes it true, never before.

**Closing probe:** cmd:python3 -m foundation standards --adopted conventional-commits-semver

**Prediction:** spec_quality >= 0.7 within 336 h (read by `python3 -m foundation specgate --report`; this item closing by its done check keeps the share of well-specified open items at or above today's reading)

**Out of scope:** rewriting working internals to carry the label, or changing the row to adopted without code and a probe.

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-26T05:33:04Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 6.1 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
